A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TAGRPO research, with readable text, equations, figures and tables. All 12 pages of v1 and 17 pages of v2 support comparison. v1 ends with references and has no appendices; v2 adds Appendices A-D.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative I2V comparisons in Tables 1-2, training curves, qualitative generations, component ablations and text-to-video experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds human evaluations, memory-bank and hyperparameter studies, additional model comparisons, diversity measurements and VBench-I2V results.

M1.justification: The trajectory-alignment objective, best/worst trajectory anchors, GRPO combination and FIFO memory bank remain unchanged. FIFO-S2 and score-driven updates are evaluated as ablation variants. Appendix C discusses possible top-/bottom-k extensions without reporting their adoption.

E1.justification: Appendix B adds VBench-I2V data for diversity evaluation and an I2V Subject benchmark score. This is a limited expansion beyond the internal dataset; the approximately 10K training pairs, 200-example TAGRPO-Bench and existing I2V/T2V task coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Appendix B and Figure 10 newly evaluate a reproduced BranchGRPO implementation against TAGRPO on Wan 2.2; v1 only cited BranchGRPO. Existing DanceGRPO and base-model comparisons remain. The expanded DPO discussion does not constitute an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Added protocols include an 18-expert human evaluation using five dimensions and five-point scales, diversity evaluation using five videos per prompt and average pairwise V-LPIPS, and I2V Subject scoring. New experiments also use Wan2.2-TI2V-5B and SkyReels-I2V, with VideoAlign scoring for the latter. The original Section 4.1 settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Sections 4.4.3-4.4.4 add memory-capacity tests at N = 4, 8 and 16, FIFO versus FIFO-S2 versus score-driven updates, and alignment-weight sensitivity at gamma = 1, 3 and 5. Appendices B and D add diversity analysis and illustrated reward-hacking failures. These substantially extend the retained component ablations and T2V generalization study.

E5.justification: Both versions report point scores and curves without repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The same-initial-noise condition is retained. v2's evaluator and generated-video counts describe added evaluation samples, not uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1-2 and Figures 1-6 retain their results. v2 adds human ratings, sensitivity and comparator curves, and Wan 2.2 base/TAGRPO scores of 0.3824/0.4086 for V-LPIPS and 0.9653/0.9667 for I2V Subject. Within new Table 3, HunyuanVideo text-video consistency is 3.73 for the base model versus 2.73 with TAGRPO, an exception to its superiority caption.

T1.justification: The flow-matching, GRPO, KL and trajectory-alignment mathematics are retained with consolidated equation numbering and formatting. Appendix C adds qualitative arguments about advantages, clipping and stability, but no new formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: trajectory alignment exploits inter-sample relationships, the memory bank improves rollout efficiency, and TAGRPO outperforms DanceGRPO for I2V post-training. The additional evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations concerning stale trajectories, reward-distribution distortion, extrema-based guidance, diversity preservation and the separate roles of FIFO updates and KL regularization. Appendix D newly identifies HPSv3-driven brightness/contrast reward hacking and discusses mitigation. v1 lacks this detailed mechanism discussion and explicit failure analysis.

D1.justification: v2 clarifies that memory capacity N stores N groups, or N times G trajectories, specifies per-step FIFO refreshes, and states that KL operates on current rollouts. It replaces general future-release promises with a project-page link for deliverables and visual comparisons; the PDFs do not establish actual code or model availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Reg-DPO, VBench++ and LPIPS, and develops focused comparisons with DPO and BranchGRPO in the appendices. The broader positioning around GRPO-based I2V post-training remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most original prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 shortens the conclusion, changes related-work subheadings and author-role text, adds an impact statement, and organizes supplementary material into Appendices A-D. The revision primarily adds scientific content rather than extensively rewriting the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the two-column format with a single-column layout, changes the title/header presentation, and rearranges existing tables and plots. It adds Figures 7-12 and Tables 3-5. The original method diagram and qualitative images are retained, despite their resizing and repositioning.

improvement.justification: The added design ablations and BranchGRPO comparison strengthen empirical scrutiny, while limited public-benchmark and human evaluations broaden validation beyond v1's internal reward-based assessment. Explicit reward-hacking examples improve transparency. These gains are tempered by missing uncertainty estimates, incompletely specified human-study procedures, and Table 3's unacknowledged text-consistency decline despite its superiority caption. The evidence supports a net improvement, but not a decisive resolution of the paper's validation weaknesses.
